column1: # equivalent_mutants.tsv - reviewed-equivalent mutants (WF2 review fix round 3). A mutant listed here is a survivor that
# cannot change observable behaviour; the runner reports it EQUIV. Columns: kind<TAB>name<TAB>detail-prefix<TAB>reason<TAB>reviewed-by.
# A row matching no mutant, or a mutant a test kills, is a STALE entry and fails the runner. Reasons are arguments, re-derived
# by the author from the DDL and (where marked) confirmed by the independent WF2 reviewer; they are not test results.

column4: Every polarity value other than RED/GREEN is already rejected: polarity is non-NULL only for red_run/green_run (the kind/polarity pairing CHECK) and those kinds each pin polarity to RED / GREEN in their own CHECKs; no input reaches this CHECK alone.

The review row is bound to the cycle twice: v.review_id > rev_hwm and ve.evidence_id > ev_hwm. A review row cannot cite evidence recorded after it (the FK needs the row to exist), so a review row older than the reopen cannot cite post-reopen evidence; dropping the review_id clause leaves the evidence clause, which excludes exactly the same rows.

The reachability select of trg_items_insert_guard (same trigger, runs first) already refuses every terminal insert whose last logged status is not Queued unless the move is an edge of the graph; for an edge from a worked-on status v_legacy_exempt is false (it excludes every item with an In progress / Ready for testing / In testing / Operator-blocked / Reopened log row). The Queued restriction in the custody select is therefore never the deciding clause.

The caught-mutation join is bound to the cycle twice: m.run_row > run_hwm and me.evidence_id > ev_hwm. A test-run row cannot cite evidence recorded after it (the FK needs the evidence row to exist), so a run row from before the reopen can never cite post-reopen evidence; dropping the run_row clause leaves the evidence clause, which excludes exactly the same rows.

The two differ only for a legacy-exempt item whose last logged status is not Queued, inserted as a terminal status that is no edge of the graph, where the second select of the same trigger would then have to pass through a live decision. A live decision needs a complete closure chain, and v_closure_ready accepts only custody_basis machine_evidence (Fixed/Implemented/Completed) or false_positive_evidence/structural_impossibility/accepted_exception (Obsolete); v_legacy_exempt requires custody_basis legacy_import. The bases are disjoint, so no live decision can exist for a legacy-exempt item and the second select refuses what the mutant lets the first select pass.

component_id is pinned by the CHECK (unit_alias GLOB 'F-'||component_id||'-*') on reg_findings: an UPDATE of component_id alone is refused by that CHECK whether or not the trigger names the column, so the column in the trigger list is redundant. Measured by the WF3 reviewer (W10: survives all three suites, edit refused anyway).
